series.title: Real wages — FSO gross wage index
series.definition: Published Swiss real gross wage index for total employees, base 1939=100, measuring CPI-adjusted wage purchasing power under the FSO wage-index methodology. This is a wage-price index, not median salary or take-home pay.
series.institutional_coverage: Employees working in Switzerland in the secondary and tertiary sectors under the Swiss Wage Index coverage; total men and women, not self-employed income or all household resources
series.aggregation: FSO-published annual real index, SEX=T, WAGE_TYPE=R, VALUE. Preserve native values rather than deflating again or deriving growth from rounded index levels. Until 1993 the CPI timing is October; from 1994 it is annual-average variation.

breaks.description: Wage source changes from the October wage survey to SSUV accident-report data; CPI timing changes from October to annual-average variation. Preserve the source-published history, not a seamless identical-method comparison.

series.usage_notes: Coverage 1942–2025. 1939 is the index base, not an extra observation. The source flags 1942 E (estimated); the atlas marks it reconstructed/source-estimated, not forecast. Subsequent A values are observed/final. This fixed-structure gross wage measure differs from household income, median pay, productivity and changes in employment mix. Source precision changes in 2021. The 1942 growth field describes the 1939–1942 average, so it is not imported as a one-year change. No full-year 2026 value.

series.title: Real median disposable household income — equivalised
series.definition: FSO-published real median disposable equivalised income for the total population in private households, without imputed rent, in CHF per month at 2023 prices. It represents household living standards adjusted for household size, not the median raw household total or a mean.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss resident population in private households, HBS/HABE, total population including people in pensioner households; person-level equivalised income, without imputed rent
series.aggregation: Annual HBS reference-year estimates expressed as monthly income amounts. Publisher CPI-deflated medians at 2023 prices are imported unchanged, not divided by the atlas CPI again, shifted to SILC interview years, multiplied into annual totals or converted using PPP.

series.usage_notes: Coverage 2000–2023. Disposable income includes transfers and deducts social insurance contributions, taxes, basic health-insurance premiums and regular transfers to other households, but not ordinary consumption/rent. Modified OECD equivalence scale: oldest person 1.0, other people aged 14+ 0.5, children under 14 0.3. No imputed rent. These HBS figures must not be spliced with SILC, working-household-only estimates, means or nominal workbook medians. Point-estimate chart; 95% bounds remain in the original source download. Small annual movements do not establish statistical significance. No invented 2024–2026 observations.

series.title: Hourly labour productivity — real output per hour
series.definition: FSO-published real output per actual hour worked for the Swiss domestic economy, index 1991=100. Measures economy-wide labour productivity, not output per worker, nominal CHF per hour, wages or individual worker performance.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss total economy, domestic production concept; FSO WPS national-accounts output and compatible actual-hours denominator
series.aggregation: Published annual productivity index: real GDP volume index divided by the compatible total actual-hours index, multiplied by 100; both source inputs have base 1991=100. Source values retained, not recalculated from a different atlas GDP vintage or from monthly averages.
series.usage_notes: Coverage 1991–2025. The FSO harmonised pre-2010 total hours following the 2021 WV revision to avoid a productivity break; do not splice unadjusted WV history or create a false 2010 gap. 2023–2025 are revised (R), not labelled provisional merely because they are recent. No partial 2026 or pre-1991 backfill. A value of 149.4 means about 49.4% more real output per hour than in 1991, not CHF 149.4/hour.

series.title: Total actual hours worked — FSO (BFS)
series.definition: Annual total actual hours worked in Swiss domestic production, in millions of hours, using the FSO WPS denominator compatible with its hourly-productivity series. A measure of labour input, not hours per employee or job.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss total economy, domestic production concept; actual total hours used by FSO Growth and productivity statistics (WPS)
series.aggregation: Published calendar-year total in millions of hours from T 04.07.04.01 column C; original numeric precision retained. The physical hours measure has no nominal or real price basis. Reconciled against the same-vintage WPS actual-hours index; revision flags come from its retained companion CSV.
series.usage_notes: Coverage 1991–2025, including source-harmonised pre-2010 hours; these differ from unadjusted Work Volume Statistics history. 2023–2025 are revised in the companion WPS CSV. Do not replace this denominator with a newer headline WV release, contract hours, hours per job or resident-only labour input. No full-year 2026 value. For example, 8088.317 million hours in 2025 is about 8.088 billion hours.

series.title: CHF/EUR exchange rate — annual mean
series.definition: Swiss francs per euro, using the ECB's published annual average of reference rates. A decrease means a stronger franc against the euro.
series.aggregation: ECB-published calendar-year average of daily reference rates; original precision retained. Not year-end, not an average of rounded monthly means.

breaks.description: Euro introduced on 1 January 1999. No pre-1999 synthetic euro observations; historical DEM is a separate series.

series.usage_notes: Lower CHF per EUR = franc appreciation. ECB reference rates are informational and differ in fixing convention from SNB quotes. Coverage 1999–2025; no partial 2026 annual mean. Reference rates are not transaction prices.

series.title: CHF/USD exchange rate — annual mean
series.definition: Swiss francs per US dollar, using the Federal Reserve's published G.5A annual average of New York noon buying rates. A decrease means a stronger franc against the dollar.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss franc against the US dollar
series.aggregation: Federal Reserve-published arithmetic average of daily noon buying rates for cable transfers in New York; not a 31 December spot rate even though the XML labels each annual period YYYY-12-31.

series.usage_notes: Lower CHF per USD = franc appreciation. New York noon buying rates differ from ECB/Frankfurt/SNB fixings. Coverage 1971–2025; no partial 2026 annual mean.

series.title: CHF/DEM historical exchange rate — annual mean
series.definition: Swiss francs per Deutsche Mark: atlas arithmetic average of daily 100/x, where x is the Bundesbank's official historical Frankfurt quotation in DEM per 100 CHF. A decrease means a stronger franc against the mark.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss franc against the Deutsche Mark, historical German fixing
series.aggregation: For each valid daily fixing x in DEM per 100 CHF, calculate 100/x CHF per DEM, then take the unweighted mean of available fixings in a complete calendar year (all 12 months, at least 200 valid fixings). Omit weekends, holidays and closures without filling. Round only the final mean to 15 significant digits. Omit incomplete 1949.

series.usage_notes: Lower CHF per DEM = franc appreciation. Atlas-calculated annual mean, not an inverse of the Bundesbank annual mean (inversion and averaging do not commute). Historical coverage 1950–1998, distinct from EUR. Frankfurt fixing differs from the other bilateral series.

series.title: CHF nominal effective exchange rate — annual mean

series.usage_notes: Higher index = nominal franc appreciation, opposite to CHF per foreign currency. Index level is not a percentage overvaluation. Nominal and real indices have distinct price bases and axes. Coverage 1973–2025; source terms permit non-commercial use.

series.title: CHF real effective exchange rate — annual mean
series.definition: SNB CPI-based real effective overall CHF exchange-rate index, 2000=100, adjusting the nominal index for consumer-price developments in Switzerland and trading partners. Higher values mean real franc appreciation.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss franc against the SNB overall trading-partner basket
series.aggregation: SNB-published yearly average, devwkieffia K/G/I, 2000=100; CPI deflation. IMF-method competition weights, two-year averages updated annually; chained Törnqvist index. Not the PPI-based variant or the euro-area-only index.

breaks.description: 1973–1999: 15 trading partners; from 2000: partners exceeding 0.2% of Swiss foreign trade selected from a 54-country pool. Retains the SNB's published backcast under the modern methodology.

series.title: Annual registered unemployment rate — SECO
series.definition: Annual registered unemployment rate (registrierte Arbeitslosenquote): arithmetic mean of twelve complete monthly, unadjusted SECO rates from the same SNB vintage. Counts RAV-registered people without a job who are immediately available, relative to the labour force. This is an atlas derivation, separate from the ILO survey rate.
series.institutional_coverage: People registered as unemployed at an RAV; rate relative to the labour force
series.aggregation: Arithmetic mean of twelve complete monthly observations; no partial-year 2026 value.
series.usage_notes: Verified derived companion: 1984–2025 complete annual means from the monthly SNB/SECO rate. The calculation is registered in transformations.json and preserves the monthly source snapshot lineage. No full-year 2026 estimate is generated. See docs/source-audit/registered-unemployment-annual.md.

series.title: Annual SNB policy rate
series.definition: Calendar-day-weighted annual mean of the administered SNB policy rate, calculated from official effective daily rates for complete years.
series.aggregation: Sum the effective rate for every calendar day, including weekends/holidays, then divide by 365 or 366. Carry the last effective policy rate until the next published change.
series.usage_notes: Calculated annual averages for 2020–2025. 2019 starts in June and 2026 ends in October, so both incomplete years are absent. This is an atlas calculation, not an SNB-published annual table. No earlier instrument is spliced in. Source observations can be corrected in later vintages.

series.title: Annual Confederation 10Y yield / historical proxy
series.definition: Annual OECD Swiss ten-year government benchmark yield from 1955, preceded by the SNB long-term Confederation yield-by-maturity proxy for 1946–1954. The proxy is an explicit historical extension, not a constant-maturity ten-year spot rate. 2026 is a partial-year average.
series.instrument: OECD ten-year government benchmark; historical Confederation bond proxy before 1955
series.maturity: 10 years from 1955; source-defined long term for 1946–1954
series.aggregation: 1946–1954: published SNB annual averages. 1955–2025: OECD annual benchmark observations. 2026: arithmetic mean of Jan–Aug OECD monthly observations (8 months), provisional partial year. Values retained at three decimals.

breaks.description: 1946–1954: historical long-term yield-by-maturity proxy; not an exact ten-year benchmark.
Switch from historical yield-by-maturity proxy to OECD ten-year government benchmark; definitions are not identical.
Partial-year average: Jan–Aug 2026 (8 months), not a full-year average or current yield.

series.usage_notes: 1946–1954 rows are marked reconstructed because of the proxy extension; their source yields are observed. 2026 is observed/provisional, not a forecast. This series differs from the daily SNB fitted spot-rate candidate. Do not pair the 2026 average with a different-month short-rate average. Data retain publisher-specific usage terms.

series.title: Annual three-month GMBF yield
series.definition: Annual average yield of three-month Confederation money market debt register claims (GMBF). SNB historical table 1980–2006, continued from monthly EG3M observations for 2007 onward. 2026 is partial-year.
series.aggregation: Unweighted average of month-end observations, using the last issue/auction in a month. Before 1990: yield at issue; since 1990: auction yield. Published annual values for 1980–2006; means of 12 EG3M observations for 2007–2025; Jan–Sep mean (9 months) for 2026. Three decimals.

breaks.description: Quotation changes from yield at issue to auction yield; last issue/auction of each month.
Continue historical published annual table with computed calendar-year means of the same SNB EG3M monthly series.
Partial-year average: Jan–Sep 2026 (9 months), not a full-year average or current yield.

series.usage_notes: No three-month observations are supplied before 1980; absence is not zero. 2026 is observed/provisional. Public SNB portal data are reused for non-commercial educational purposes with attribution; commercial reuse may require consent.

series.title: General government gross debt / GDP
series.definition: Swiss general government gross debt as a percentage of nominal GDP. Composite of JST/HSSO historical ratios for 1946–1987, JST-compiled IMF ratios for 1988–1989 and the April 2026 IMF WEO table for 1990–2026. The early aggregation and modern IMF liability/consolidation conventions differ; source changes are explicit. This is not the narrower Maastricht debt ratio.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss general government; historical Confederation, cantons and municipalities, modern IMF general-government coverage
series.instrument: Gross government debt; historical and IMF definitions differ
series.aggregation: Annual gross debt stock divided by annual nominal GDP; 2026 is an IMF forecast
series.source_identifier: JST R6 CHE debtgdp (1946–1989); IMF WEO April 2026 GGXWDG_NGDP (1990–2026)

breaks.description: JST changes from HSSO U.45 total debt / historical GDP to IMF WEO public debt / GDP. Coverage, liability and consolidation conventions may differ; do not interpret the splice as a seamless constant-definition series.
Continue JST 1988–1989 IMF vintage with April 2026 WEO history. Source vintage and precision change; the two-year JST bridge is not revised with the current WEO data.

series.usage_notes: Not Maastricht debt and not Confederation-only debt. No pre-1946 total-government observations are imported from JST because earlier JST debt covers central government only. 1946–1987 is marked reconstructed; 2025 is observed/provisional and 2026 forecast/provisional (38.50% of GDP), not a completed observation. Historical ratios retain the supplied one-decimal rounding; modern ratios retain the cited two-decimal table. Historical data/adaptations: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 with JST citation; modern data retain IMF and ecolod terms. Reuse this combined file for non-commercial purposes under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, retaining all source attributions.

series.title: Confederation debt / GDP
series.definition: Federal Finance Administration FS gross-debt ratio for the Confederation, published in the main aggregate export as bruttoschuldenquote and converted from a fraction to percent.
series.aggregation: Annual end-of-period ratio from the publisher's aggregate export; 2026 is a forecast/highrechnung, not a completed-year observation.
series.source_identifier: main_extern / hh=bund / model=gfs / variable=bruttoschuldenquote / fraction converted to percent
series.usage_notes: Verified publisher ratio from the FFA export, retained separately from the atlas's general-government debt/GDP composite. The source codelist documents the surrounding FS/GFS concepts; this export variable is selected directly and converted to percentage points. 2025 is a Rechnung observation and 2026 is Hochrechnung.

series.title: Confederation 10Y − 3M spread
series.definition: Difference between matched completed-calendar-year Confederation ten-year benchmark and three-month GMBF annual-average yields, 1980–2025.
series.instrument: Ten-year government benchmark minus three-month GMBF
series.aggregation: Left annual yield minus right annual yield, in percentage points, after input values are rounded to three decimals. Matched completed years only; 2026 excluded because input averaging windows differ.

breaks.description: Quotation changes from yield at issue to auction yield; last issue/auction of each month.

series.usage_notes: Negative values indicate annual-average short yields above long yields; annual averages do not establish the duration of intrayear inversion. 2026 has no spread observation because Jan–Aug and Jan–Sep means are not comparable. Native source terms are inherited.

series.title: Historical SNB discount rate — year end
series.definition: Published year-end official discount rate, in percent; historical instrument distinct from Libor targets and the modern policy rate.
series.aggregation: Published year-end readings; no annual average or effective-date interpolation.
series.usage_notes: 92 year-end values, 1907–1998. Blank 1999–2006 table entries remain absent. The historical discount instrument is not joined into Libor targets or modern policy rates. The original source is a PDF; the committed CSV is a checked transcription of its figures.

series.title: Historical SNB Lombard rate — year end
series.definition: Published year-end official Lombard credit rate, in percent; historical instrument distinct from discount credit, Libor targets and the modern policy rate.
series.aggregation: Published year-end readings; no annual average or effective-date interpolation.

breaks.description: From May 1989 the Lombard rate was calculated daily from a money-market rate rather than being tied to the discount rate. The publication gives conflicting margin descriptions; no homogeneous margin is assumed.
Published transitional Lombard readings equal the special-rate repo facility in 2004–2005. Lombard credit was abolished at the end of 2005.

series.usage_notes: 99 year-end values, 1907–2005. The blank 2006 Lombard entry remains absent. These are published year-end readings, not annual averages or an uninterrupted homogeneous policy-rate instrument. The CSV is a checked transcription of the source PDF. Table footnote and narrative disagree on the post-May-1989 margin; preserve the figures without inferring a margin.

series.title: Five-year fixed mortgage offer rate — annual mean
series.definition: Annual mean of the SNB unweighted cross-bank averages of published five-year fixed mortgage rates at twelve month-ends. An offered new-business rate, not a negotiated transaction rate or the average cost of existing mortgages.
series.institutional_coverage: Banks in the SNB published-rate survey, Switzerland
series.aggregation: Arithmetic mean of twelve complete calendar-year month-end published-rate means. December 2007 is retained in the source but excluded as a partial first year.
series.usage_notes: 2008–2025 only. No full-year 2026. Unweighted across banks and months; not weighted by mortgage amounts or loan originations. Do not splice with historical cantonal variable first-mortgage rates or actual new-loan agreements.

series.title: Outstanding mortgage average rate — annual mean
series.definition: Arithmetic mean of the four BWO survey-date volume-weighted average interest rates on existing domestic CHF mortgages. Measures the stock of outstanding contracts, including old fixed-rate loans, not current offers.
series.institutional_coverage: Domestic CHF mortgage claims of reporting banks in Switzerland; property collateral in Switzerland
series.instrument: Volume-weighted average interest rate on outstanding mortgages
series.aggregation: Mean of the March, June, September and December survey-date averages. December readings published the next March belong to the survey year. Each quarter has equal weight; no annual mortgage-volume weights are available.
series.usage_notes: 2009–2025. Do not align underlying averages to the reference rate effective dates, round them to quarter-points or infer a new-mortgage offer rate. The first source year 2008 lacks Q1 and is omitted. December 2025 uses the observation released in March 2026.

series.title: Rental reference interest rate — annual mean
series.definition: Calendar-day-weighted annual mean of the official BWO mortgage reference rate legally in force. This descriptive annual statistic is not itself a legally applicable reference rate or a measure of market rents.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss national mortgage-based rental reference rate
series.aggregation: For every calendar day, use the published reference rate from its effective date until the next effective date; sum and divide by 365 or 366 days. Announcements beyond year-end bound carry-forward, not a forecast.

breaks.description: From 2 December 2011, commercial rounding of the underlying average to the nearest quarter-point replaces the original threshold rule. The annual mean includes both rules.

series.usage_notes: 2009–2025; 2008 began on 10 September and is not a full year. Preserve historical published values rather than applying current rounding retrospectively. For legal rental adjustments use the official effective-date rate and applicable law, never this statistical annual mean.

series.title: Real residential property prices — annual mean
series.definition: Annual mean of four quarterly BIS CPI-deflated Swiss residential property price index values, 2010=100. A long-run national composite with distinct offer-price, transaction-price and FSO statistical segments.
series.institutional_coverage: Swiss residential property, owner-occupied flats/houses historically; all dwellings from 2017
series.aggregation: Arithmetic mean of four complete quarterly real index observations. BIS has already divided nominal property prices by the Swiss CPI and set the 2010 mean to 100. No second deflation or rebasing.

breaks.description: BIS historical input changes from offer prices to transaction prices for the unweighted average of flats and houses.
BIS input changes to FSO all-dwellings residential property prices from 2017-Q1; earlier flat/house composites remain historical reconstructions.

series.usage_notes: 1970–2025. Historical composite years through 2016 are identified as reconstructed; documentation describes a best-effort long history, not homogeneous directly observed transactions. Source 2026-Q1/Q2 are retained for audit but no annual 2026 is published. Not a CHF price, rental index, affordability measure or property total return.

series.title: Private non-financial credit / GDP — year-end
series.definition: BIS break-adjusted credit to Swiss households and non-financial corporations from all lenders, divided by its compatible four-quarter nominal GDP, selected at Q4. Before 1999-Q4 the source uses domestic bank credit as a historical proxy.
series.institutional_coverage: Resident households including NPISH and non-financial corporations, including public corporations; all lenders from 1999-Q4
series.instrument: Core debt: loans, debt securities and currency/deposits where applicable; gross and unconsolidated
series.aggregation: Use the published Q4 credit-to-GDP ratio. Numerator is the end-quarter credit stock; denominator is the sum of the last four quarters of nominal GDP in the same BIS vintage. Neither an annual average of ratios nor a ratio using atlas GDP.

breaks.description: Historical domestic-bank-credit proxy changes from IMF IFS inputs from 1975-Q2.
1981-Q4 change in historical bank-claims compilation; earlier claims exclude precious-metal accounts.
1987-Q4 change in estimation of private domestic bank credit from bank claims and government/bank exclusions.
From 1999-Q4 quarterly financial accounts replace the narrower domestic-bank-credit proxy. Earlier years are reconstructed/proxy history despite BIS break adjustments.
Cross-border capital-linkage survey revised and securities survey reporting population expanded; BIS series is break-adjusted.

series.usage_notes: 1960–2025. Market-value convention applies to debt securities; loans are valued nominally. Gross, unconsolidated debt is not net household debt, bank-only credit, the credit-to-GDP gap or a debt-service burden. BIS break adjustment cannot remove all coverage changes. No 2026 year-end ratio is inferred.

series.title: Domestic mortgage loans outstanding — year-end
series.definition: December stock of domestic mortgage loans utilised by non-banks at banks in Switzerland, in nominal CHF millions. Includes mortgage claims in mortgage-loan and fair-value balance-sheet positions. Not new mortgage originations or unused credit limits.
series.institutional_coverage: Banks in Switzerland; domestic non-bank mortgage borrowers, all maturities
series.aggregation: Select each December month-end stock unchanged. Do not sum or average monthly balances. December 1985 is available despite the source starting in June that year.

breaks.description: June 1997 reporting-population expansion. Earlier all-bank aggregates were extrapolated where possible; atlas identifies pre-1997 annual stocks as reconstructed.
From November 2001 utilisation is the gross claim rather than the earlier balance-sheet figure.
September 2006 includes all Raiffeisen banks, rather than only the 34 larger banks.
PostFinance included from June 2013.
May 2017 intragroup-financing arrangements changed; retain source warning.

series.usage_notes: 1985–2025. Nominal year-end stock, not inflation-adjusted or scaled to GDP. Not restricted to households or owner-occupied dwellings; mortgage loans can finance other domestic collateral. Source revisions and reporting changes limit comparisons. The credit-lines-only clarification and suppression of bank subgroups do not create artificial gaps in this selected utilisation total.
